momentum: The arc keeps its promise. 02 pays the cover straight away ('The vote moved. The work didn't.'), 03 defines what is being voted on, 04 gives the number, 05 puts in the human counterweight, 06 brings the dissent, 07 sets out the order, 08 synthesises and 09 asks one clean question. The middle doesn't escalate, though. 06 is the conflict beat ('probably going to be messy') but it is drawn as the same blue hillshade panel as 02, so the peak doesn't feel like a peak. The 'who drew the first draft?' plant for 03 to 04 isn't on 03's page. The reader gets there by the four-page link and not by an open question.

continuity: The edge-tease from 01 to 02 lands: exit and entry heights match. The route-head motif follows the state table on 01, 02, 03 (tiny gold datum tick), 04 (surviving rail), 06 (path stops at UAA), 07 (NOVEMBER station), 08 (gold open ring) and 09 (Polaris). The breaks: (1) the 05 gold thread has a findable loose end at display (812, 1780) above the fixture band. It starts off the right edge, bends twice and stops on nothing, so it reads as a stray line, not as the route passing through. (2) The February ring is meant to stay open and unchanged, but 09 adds a crosshair inside it, which reads as a state change ('targeted'). (3) On 07 the campus bundle leaves the trunk above the NOVEMBER station, between OCTOBER and NOVEMBER, so the branch reads as starting before the gold 'now' point.
rhythm: The breather lands at 05 as planned. But the frames either side form two runs of three dense slides: 02, 03, 04 (each 4 to 5 body lines plus a full art panel) and 06, 07, 08 (4, 3 plus a six-station timeline, 4). 04 is where it starts to tire: the third dense block in a row, with a legend to decode. Cut 03's body to two sentences (drop 'UA says it sets six...', since the ring labels already carry 6/4/5) and that run breaks.
consistency: The fixtures hold: wordmark, mono footer, coordinates and counters 01/09, 02/09, 03/09, 04/09, 05/09, 06/09, 07/09, 08/09, 09/09 are all present and correct. 09 swaps the small wordmark for the large one, which is acceptable for a close. Palette and type hold across 01, 02 and 04 to 09. 03 is the frame that looks pasted from another deck: warm grey clay-like granite in a 3D still life, with a key at azimuth 222 against the deck's 175 to 200. Light direction is close enough elsewhere. COPY CHECK: the Manrope body apostrophes render curly in 03 'doesn't', 04 'UA's', 06 'it's' and 07 'Claude's', while the headlines' 'didn't' and 'UAA's' are straight. If those are U+2019 in copy.json, they break the straight-quotes house rule. Verify and normalise.

weakest_frames.fix: Delete the hachure coast ghost. Its tick clusters read as fur or burrs on the sheet, at display y 1080 to 1820, most of all the bottom strip at y 1750 to 1820. Replace it with one continuous cased coastline (or a graded low-alpha hillshade ghost) at 0.12 alpha. That also gives the dead lower-right quadrant (x 850 to 1500, y 1450 to 1820) modelled tone, where it now has only stray fur flecks.

Re-model the boulder, the largest object. It reads as smeared clay: the whole rock is defocused, not just the shard, so the sharp cap looks pasted on. A black annulus of decal or shadow around the cap is a findable reserve edge. Keep the boulder sharp within about 0.15 m of the cap with crisp feldspar speckle and a real terminator, and replace the black ring with a soft contact gradient. The black band between the body and the rock (display y 950 to 1150) is also a dead region. Carry the lit sun pool and haze up into it.

Hide the terrain plane's edges. A lighter navy trapezoid edge shows at upper right (display x 1480 to 1600, y 960 to 1350) and a curved mesh boundary along the bottom (y 1780 to 1850). Extend the plane past the frustum and fog it to the sky colour. Then lift western Alaska, which is barely modelled, so the lower-left half isn't a dim slab.

The breather is allowed to be quiet, but the stipple is sparse scatter, not a glow, and the lower third is a coast line plus a gold stub. Raise the core density and add the planned two-part halo so Anchorage reads as light. End the gold thread off an edge rather than in mid-air.

The Gulf below the coast is flat black across the lower right of the lower third (display x 700 to 1300, y 1500 to 1800). Paint the planned sea gloss and low-sun streak there, and sharpen the relief so the Alaska Range reads as ridgelines, not as cotton-ball mottling.

cross_frame: Cause a, census: AKS.loadDEM appears on 1, 2, 3, 4, 5, 6, 8 and 9. It is a data loader feeding five different kinds of mark-making (PBR mesh, hillshade, 3D skyline, contour engraving, stipple and outline), so it does not read as the same drawing on the sheet. Not cause a.

Near-repeats, each kept to two frames (under the limit): the PBR whole-state mesh from above on 01 and 08 (very similar framing, the closest the deck comes to 'the same drawing'), the hillshade panel on 02 and 06 (same panel frame and blue ramp), and the contour engraving on 04 and 09. If 08 is re-rendered, change the camera to a low oblique so it stops echoing the cover.

Cause d appears on three frames: fur hachure on 07, the black annulus on 03, mesh plane edges on 08. Also check the stair-stepped coastline pixels on 06 around Knik Arm (display about 830, 1100 to 1160).

No frame meets 'masterful real depth'. 03 was declared the masterful depth frame, but its depth stack falls apart: rock and shard are equally blurred, there is a dead band between ground and sky, and the cap sits on a black disc. This alone keeps the deck below 8.
craft.tonal_arc: The census passes and matches what I see: 01 13, 02 12, 03 22 (peak, as declared), 04 11, 05 8 (darkest, as declared), 06 12, 07 9, 08 12, 09 9, span 13.3 L*. The miss it can't measure: apart from the spike at 03, the deck is one flat band of navy at L* 9 to 13. 03's peak is warm grey granite, off palette for the deck, not a lit object inside the deck's world. No frame after 03 has a lit focal object, though 08's ring glow could be one. So the 'arc' is a single spike, not a shape.
